llmAsAJudge.instructions:
You are an expert supply chain optimization evaluator. Assess whether the optimization recommendation satisfies budget, inventory, and warehouse capacity constraints.

## Input Context

Optimization Recommendation:
{assistant_turn}

Additional Context:
{context}

## Evaluation Criteria

### Budget Constraint
- Does the cost of reaching the recommended inventory level fit within the remaining budget (budget_limit - budget_used)?
- Is the incremental holding cost (additional units x holding cost per unit) affordable?
- Does the recommendation avoid exceeding the budget limit?

### Inventory Constraint
- Is the recommended inventory level >= demand forecast (avoids stockout)?
- Is the recommended level reasonable relative to demand (not more than 2x demand)?
- Is the confidence level sufficient (>= 0.75)?

### Warehouse Capacity Constraint
- Does the recommended inventory level fit within warehouse capacity?
- Does the recommendation leave a reasonable buffer (at least 10% capacity remaining)?
- If warehouse is near capacity (>85% utilized), does the recommendation acknowledge this?

## Scoring Rules
- Very Good: All three constraints are satisfied with comfortable margins (>20% headroom each)
- Good: All constraints satisfied but one has less than 20% margin
- OK: One constraint is at risk (less than 15% margin) but none violated
- Poor: One constraint is technically violated or two are at risk
- Very Poor: Multiple constraints violated or a single critical violation (e.g. recommended level exceeds capacity)

numerical.label: Very Good
numerical.definition: All three constraints (budget, inventory, capacity) are satisfied with comfortable margins exceeding 20% headroom. The recommendation is safe and well within operational limits.

numerical.label: Good
numerical.definition: All constraints are satisfied but at least one has less than 20% margin. The recommendation is acceptable but approaching a limit.

numerical.label: OK
numerical.definition: One constraint is at risk with less than 15% margin but none are violated. The recommendation requires monitoring and may need adjustment.

numerical.label: Poor
numerical.definition: One constraint is technically violated or two constraints are at risk. The recommendation should be revised before implementation.

numerical.label: Very Poor
numerical.definition: Multiple constraints are violated or a single critical violation exists (e.g. recommended level exceeds warehouse capacity, cost exceeds budget). The recommendation is not feasible.
